---
title: Home
---

This example demonstrates **project-scoped artifact sharing**. The
theme CSS (Bootstrap + Quarto's defaults compiled together) is
identical for every page; rather than write a copy next to each
page's HTML, Quarto writes it **once** to
`_site/site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-<hash>.css` and points every
page's `<head>` at that single file.

The clever part is that `<link rel="stylesheet">` hrefs are
**relativized to each page's depth**:

- From `_site/index.html` (root), the link reads
  `site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-<hash>.css`.
- From `_site/docs/api.html` (one deep), the link reads
  `../site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-<hash>.css`.
- From `_site/docs/internals/architecture.html` (two deep), the
  link reads `../../site_libs/quarto/quarto-theme-<hash>.css`.

Same shared file, three different relative paths. This is the work
of the project-scoped artifact store — every artifact has a
**scope** (`Page` or `Project`) and a resolver that turns
`(scope, path, current_page)` into the right URL.
